current.text: Jaylen Brown is gone from Boston. Jayson Tatum and Paul George take his place, and Paul George is the clear number two option behind Tatum.
He came off the bench in a preseason game.

Experts project him as the sixth man and main backup ball handler, not a starter. One expert says a 29-minute bench role may suit him better than a 32-minute starting role. He could start if Mike Conley handles the backup point guard job.
Experts see him as the third usage option at best, and maybe the fourth, behind Tatum, George and Derrick White. His usage path is more crowded than last season.
Experts reject the idea of a Jalen Brunson-style breakout. He had about 21 to 22 percent usage last season even with few teammates around. He turns 29 soon.
Experts expect a step back from last season, at around 17 to 18 points per game. They say he has basically peaked.
His strong numbers without Jaylen Brown last season came without Tatum and George on the floor, so experts say they do not carry over.

Most experts call him a bust or a fade at his ADP of about 75 to 81. One worst case puts him at 171st, and he could finish outside the top 110 to 120. In auctions, Josh sees him as worth no more than 4 USD.
His draft spot in mock drafts ranges from the 70s to 100. He went for 6 USD in one auction mock.
If Paul George only plays about 30 games, Pritchard would step back into last season's bigger role.
One expert expects his two-point percentage to recover to about 59 percent. He also thinks Tatum and George, who share the ball more than Jaylen Brown did, could help his shot quality.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league, with three of them in our playoff window. Its playoff schedule through March 28 is 4-3-4 games, one short of the maximum.
Boston is very deep, with at least 12 rotation-level players, and is projected to win about 48 games.

durable.text: He is a streaky bucket-getter who can score 40 on a hot night but also has cold nights. He is elite on two-pointers in the paint outside the restricted area.
He blocks almost no shots, even for a guard.

note: The market price looks right and our league's old price looks too high. Average costs are 3.9 USD on Yahoo and 3.0 USD on ESPN, and Josh caps him at 4 USD. Our league paid 16 USD last season, and Yahoo values him at 13 USD, so bid in the single digits and do not chase him near those numbers. He fits punt BLK guard builds: his projections show about 2.8 threes, good FT% and assists, and few turnovers. He has also played 79 to 82 games in each of the last three seasons. Early in the season, check whether he starts or comes off the bench, whether his minutes stay near 30, and how much usage he keeps next to Tatum and George. If Paul George misses time, his value goes up.
